body: I feel like we should specify the effect that this will have. For example, what happens if the port was already open? What happens if `open()` is called after this? Intuitively I think this should have the same effect as if the port was disconnected. That is, it is an ungraceful termination of the site's connection to the device and might even fire a `disconnect` event. It could also be an error to call this method if the port is open.

    + It is posssible to voluntarily revoke a permission to a serial port that was granted by a user. + + 
    +        // Request a serial port.
+        const port = await navigator.serial.requestPort();
+
+        // Then later... revoke permission to the serial port.
+        await port.forget();
+
    +

      +
    1. Let |promise| be [=a new promise=]. +
    2. Set [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[state]]}} to `"forgetting"`. +
    3. + If [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[readable]]}} is not `null`, invoke + [=ReadableStream/cancel=] on [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[readable]]}}. +
    4. + If [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[writable]]}} is not `null`, invoke + [=WritableStream/abort=] on [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[writable]]}}. +
    5. + Remove [=this=] from the sequence of available serial ports on + the system which the user has allowed the site to access as the + result of a previous call to {{Serial/requestPort()}}. +
    6. Set [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[state]]}} to `"forgotten"`.
body: The specification should probably mention the possibility that forgetting a device is not possible (e.g. permission was granted by administrator policy). Whether in that case the device is still put into the `"forgotten"` state is an interesting question. I think it probably shouldn't be because it'll be weird for `getPorts()` to be returning a `SerialPort` instance that is otherwise unusable. Alternatively we could keep track of forgotten ports and hide them until the page reloads. That seems more complex though perhaps less surprising for the developer. What do you think?

    2. Set [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[state]]}} to `"forgetting"`. +
    3. + If [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[readable]]}} is not `null`, invoke + [=ReadableStream/cancel=] on [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[readable]]}}. +
    4. + If [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[writable]]}} is not `null`, invoke + [=WritableStream/abort=] on [=this=].{{SerialPort/[[writable]]}}.
body: Invoking `readable.cancel()` and `writable.abort()` requires the streams to be unlocked, which is basically the same thing as taking the "port must be closed to `forget()`" option I mentioned on the Chromium CL. Doing this without requiring the streams to be unlocked requires tying this algorithm in with the underlying source and sink algorithms so we can interrupt a pending operation and inject an error. I think that's a reasonable option (just add something like "if port.[[state]] becomes "forgotten" then..." to the algorithms) but it does mean we have to answer the "what if it can't be forgotten" question.
